newsitem.title: USA: AT&T says Telstar 401 satellite permanently down.
newsitem.headline: AT&T says Telstar 401 satellite permanently down.

text.p: AT&T Corp. said Friday it has been unsuccessful in re-establishing contact with Telstar 401 and has declared the communications satellite permanently out of service.

The satellite's telemetry and communications equipment stopped working early last Saturday morning, the company said. AT&T said it immediately restored service for customers whose contracts called for transfer of their transponder service to the Telstar 402R satellite, and restored other services as well.
AT&T said it is working closely with Lockheed Martin Corp., the manufacturer of Telstar 401 satellite, to determine the cause of the problem.

It will also petition the Federal Communications Commission to move the Telstar 302 satellite to Telstar 401's orbital slot at 97 degrees west longitude to provide temporary transponder capacity for customers.

Telstar 5, which is under construction by Space Systems/Loral, is scheduled to be launched in May, and will be the permanent replacement for Telstar 302 at 97 degrees west longitude, subject to FCC approval, ATT said.

An agreement had been reached on Sept. 25, 1996, to sell the AT&T Skynet Satellite Services, of which the Telstar satellites are part, to Loral Space & Communications Ltd. Both companies said in a statement that they are committed to the transaction and are holding discussions on terms of the sale.
